related.title: Using CPF for housing: Home buying guide for members above 55
related.text:
Consider using a mix of cash and CPF to pay for the purchase price and loan (if eligible). Every dollar less you spend from your CPF account on your home is at least a dollar more for your retirement.

If you qualify for a loan and intend to use CPF, keep your monthly instalments within your Ordinary Account contribution. Consider keeping 6 months of your monthly instalment in your Ordinary Account as a buffer.

CPF savings can be used for the purchase price, housing loan, stamp and legal fees.

If you are aged 55 and above and selling your current flat, the CPF refunds will first be used to top up your Retirement Account up to your Full Retirement Sum. The remaining refunds will be retained in your Ordinary Account.

You can check the amount available for use on your Home ownership dashboard, including the exact amount that you would need to refund to your CPF account upon the sale of your current flat that can be reused for your next flat.

If you are buying a resale flat, use our **Housing Usage Calculator** to estimate the amount of CPF savings you may use based on the flat's remaining lease.

Apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter to find out if you can purchase a new or resale flat, as well as the amounts of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan you are eligible for.

Note that if you are buying a short-lease flat, such as a 2-room Flexi flat or a Community Care Apartment, you are not eligible for housing loans.

You can book an appointment to visit an HDB Branch. You may also wish to contact HDB via their Write to Us.

citations.text: The SPR quota ensures that SPR families can better integrate into the local community. Malaysians are excluded from this quota because of their close cultural and historical similarities with Singaporeans. Non-Malaysian SPR households applying to buy an HDB resale flat need to be within the SPR quota for the block (8%) and neighbourhood (5%).

related.title: Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) and SPR quota: Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) and Singapore Permanent Resident Quota > How the EIP and SPR quota work
related.text:
The EIP quota applies for the purchase of an HDB flat. In addition, non-Malaysian SPR households must meet the SPR quota.

You may be eligible to buy a flat if:

- You and the flat seller are of the same ethnic group and household citizenship; or
- After your flat purchase, the number of households of your ethnic group remains within the block and neighbourhood limits. In addition, for non-Malaysian SPR households, the number of SPR households remains within the SPR quota.

- Your housing needs, e.g. to live near parents’ or child’s home, place of work, schools, etc.

related.text:
9 Procedure in granting and exercising the Option to Purchase
The procedure for entering into a binding contract for a resale transaction is as follows:
a. Sellers grant the OTP
The sellers grant an OTP to the buyers to purchase the flat at the agreed resale price and for an Option
Period of 21 days during which the sellers cannot sell the flat or make an offer to other buyers. The OTP
must be signed by all the sellers (on page 8 of the OTP) before it is granted to the buyers. The sellers
must check that they have a valid Intent to Sell and have waited out the 7-day cooling-off period, and the
buyers have a valid HFE Letter before granting them the OTP.
b. Buyers pay the Option Fee
In exchange, the buyers pay an Option Fee (preferably in a cheque) to the sellers. The buyers have up
to 21 days to exercise the OTP. During that period, the buyers can apply for a bank’s Letter of Offer (if
they are getting a bank loan) or make other arrangements/enquiries relating to the purchase.
c. Buyers exercise the OTP
If the buyers decide to purchase the flat, the buyers must exercise the OTP within the Option Period. To
exercise the OTP, the buyers must do the following:
(i) sign the Acceptance portion in page 8 of the OTP (if the buyers are getting a bank loan, the buyers
must ensure that the date of issue of the bank’s Letter of Offer is before the date of Acceptance),
(ii) deliver the signed OTP to the Sellers*, and
(iii) pay a sum called the Option Exercise Fee to the Sellers.
The Acceptance must be signed by all the buyers. For record purposes, the buyers are advised to obtain
a signed acknowledgement from the sellers on the buyer's copy of the Acceptance, stating the date and
time of exercise of the Option.

<u>First-timer couples and families</u>

To be eligible for the EHG, you must meet the following conditions:

- **Citizenship:** Singapore Citizen, and include at least 1 other Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident in the HFE letter application
- **Age:** At least 21 years old
- **Monthly household income ceiling**: $9,000
- **Employment:** Have worked continuously for at least 12 months and are working at the time of the HFE letter application. When assessing your eligibility, HDB looks at your employment over a 12-month assessment period. This 12-month period is computed as at 2 months before the month you submit your HFE letter application. For example, if you submitted your HFE letter application in May 2025, the assessment period will be from April 2024 to March 2025.
- **Property ownership:** Must not own or have an interest in any private residential property (local or overseas) and must not have disposed of one in the last 30 months before your HFE application.
- **Check out more** eligibility conditions for the EHG, for first-timer couples and families**.**

*Note: If you’re a couple comprising a first timer and a second timer, you may qualify for an EHG (Singles) grant of up to $60,000. Half of your household’s average gross monthly income must not exceed $4,500.*

related.title: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG): Enhanced CPF Housing Grant for Singles
related.text:
Learn about the eligibility conditions for singles to apply for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant.

If you are a first-timer applicant buying a flat on your own or with your non-resident spouse, you may be eligible for an Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) (Singles) to help with your new or resale flat purchase.

From 20 August 2024, first-timer singles may qualify for an EHG (Singles) of up to $60,000. If you are buying with other first-timer single(s), up to 2 singles may each be eligible for an EHG (Singles), i.e., a total of up to $120,000.

If you are buying a resale flat, you must first qualify for the CPF Housing Grant for Resale Flats (Singles) before you may be eligible for the EHG. You may also apply for the Proximity Housing Grant (PHG) (Singles) if you meet the eligibility conditions.

Apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter via the HDB Flat Portal for a holistic understanding of your housing and financing options before you embark on your home buying journey. It will inform you upfront of your eligibility to buy a new or resale flat, as well as the amount of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan you are eligible for.

- The total amount of CPF savings that can be used for your flat purchase and/ or paying monthly mortgage instalments will depend on the extent the remaining lease of the flat can cover the youngest buyer up to the age of 95.
